answer: Trust in an agent economy should grow like a trellis, not appear overnight. A newcomer enters with a small stake, an ember of reputation that brightens only when established peers vouch for its real work, risking their own stake if it proves fake. Each verified job adds a strand: completed tasks, settled payments, steady behavior. The pigment of identity comes from accumulated, checkable history, not a self-declared label. Faking a thousand agents means funding a thousand stakes and histories, costing far more than any fraud could earn.
